# Phase 34.4 native-host scripted answers

Use equivalent briefs under `claude -p` and `codex exec --sandbox workspace-write`.
When the inherited approval mode is automatic review, use `codex exec --approve-for-me`
instead: this CLI option itself selects workspace-write plus automatic review and
is mutually exclusive with `--sandbox`. Record the resolved authority and each review.
Each arm starts in a fresh scratch repository. Record the exact executable, version,
argv, source commit, plugin manifest digest, scratch identity, and `AuthorityEnvelope`.
The authority is filesystem `workspace-write`, network `inherited`, approvals `inherited`.
Permission or sandbox bypass options are forbidden. Do not widen inherited authority,
write outside scratch, contact product remotes, or perform unrecorded external actions.

## Common answers

Project: greenfield-proof. TypeScript library/CLI; npm; mobile: none; non-Blade.
Audience: developers importing a greeting function and invoking its CLI. The first
release exports a typed greeting and CLI with passing tests. No authentication,
external service, deployment, or product remote. Preserve unknowns explicitly.
Use the installed greenfield and roadmap plugin contracts and library-cli manifest.
Read the templates and references; do not substitute invented config keys or omit
promised homes. Existing brownfield homes and generated harness blocks are immutable.

## First invocation: proposal only

Read the fixture and run only the named `roadmap config capabilities --json`
compatibility command. Do not invoke `roadmap init` in any form, including
`roadmap init --help`, before approval. Read static source or top-level help for
syntax. Do not write or run a generator. Produce a complete Artifact / Target / Reason proposal, including every
command, dependency/network action, home, gate, and catalog repair. Also emit one
JSON object `{"type":"proposal","artifacts":[],"commands":[],"gates":{}}` with
concrete populated values. Its gates have exactly lint, types, unit, integration,
build, e2e, emit. Each non-none gate has an executable command; each absent gate has
a reason. Validate those keys before requesting approval. Do not emit an approval
event yourself. Stop and await the next invocation.

## Driver approval and execution

The driver checks the complete proposal and unchanged initial tree, then records the
approval response: `APPROVE GREENFIELD PLAN` as a separate input event.
Resume the same host session with that exact standalone input. The prior proposal
is the approved path/command allowlist; do not bundle new instructions into approval.
If the proposal fails validation, issue no approval and capture the failed arm.
If any preapproval mutation occurs, STOP immediately without deleting or reverting
it. Only the outer evidence driver may quarantine the failed scratch tree; an
agent cleanup cannot erase the failure.

Execute only approved operations. Emit `WRITE:` diagnostics for traceability, but
success requires raw native tool events and independently observed file snapshots;
model-authored diagnostics alone are insufficient. Run every non-none gate separately as `cd '<scratch>' && <configured command>`
and retain raw command/cwd/exit evidence. Here `<scratch>` is the absolute observed
consumer directory and `<configured command>` is its exact config binding. Stop on permission denial,
missing sibling, invalid schema, changed existing home, or failing command.

Required empty artifacts include PRD, both ADRs, CODE-STYLE, architecture index,
UX canon, harness adapters, README, archetype outputs, catalog checker, and the one
resolved roadmap config. Brownfield receipts separately account for each missing
home, preserve original homes byte-identically, and mechanically constrain the diff
to approved gaps. Test migrated docs/roadmap, explicit root override, and ambiguous
dual-marked roots without creating a second configuration.

## Repeated invocation

second run: audit the completed tree. Require zero proposals, zero writes, and an
identical final tree hash. Emit exactly one native assistant JSON result
`{"type":"audit-result","proposals":[],"writes":[],"gaps":[]}` only if the audit
finds no remaining gaps; retain actual findings otherwise. Record a separate raw
transcript and tool events. Generate
the human report from validated receipts only. Missing, failed, stale, copied, or
incomplete native evidence remains blocking; never author a replacement receipt.

## Source and evidence driver

Freeze all source inputs before starting the four fresh arms. Obtain the invocation
base and complete dirty/untracked source digest from
`plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-evidence-source.mjs`.
Pass `sourceRoot`, `invocationBaseCommit`, and `sourceSnapshotSha256` in every
observer request alongside `scratch`, `evidence`, `argv`, `stage`, and `timeout`.
Use `greenfield-native-observer.py` in the same directory to launch each request;
it checks source before and after and records transient filesystem mutations.
Keep `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` so read-only Git inspection does not refresh the index.
Propose scratch-local `.npm-cache/` and `.npm-logs/` paths when npm needs them;
include those settings in approved commands. Do not commit inside native fixtures.

After each stage finishes, run `greenfield-native-driver.mjs capture <host>
<stage-directory>` before resuming. The driver copies the native session and
checks identity, authority, command events, snapshots, and proposal structure.
Use separate `proposal`, `execution`, and `rerun` directories below each arm's
`dry-runs/evidence/` directory; never overwrite a failed attempt. Supply `arm.json`
with `host`, `kind`, absolute `scratchRoot`, unique `scratchIdentity`, discovered
`executable`, actual `version`, and brownfield `existingHomePaths`.
After all stages, `greenfield-native-driver.mjs project <empty-claude-arm>
<empty-codex-arm> <brownfield-claude-arm> <brownfield-codex-arm>` validates the
full proof before writing receipts and their Markdown projection. Angle-bracket
arguments denote the four retained arm directories, in the displayed order.
Missing evidence or any failed assertion blocks projection.

## Fixture-selected catalog check

Select the comparator before launching, using `selectCatalogCheck` from the native
evidence module and the reconciliation owner `skills/brownfield-audit/references/readme-reconcile.md`
(relative to the installed greenfield plugin root). For the empty `library-cli`
fixture, bind prospective project-root mode and project name `greenfield-proof`;
verify the generated package identity after execution. For the existing Nx fixture,
bind `node scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs --catalog emitted/repo-catalog.json`
and the existing emitted catalog's byte digest. A workspace wrapper package name
is not the identity of its multiple catalog projects. Refuse missing/malformed
required catalogs; preserve the selected catalog bytes throughout the arm.
Persist `catalogCheck` identically in arm metadata and every observer request.
Include its exact command once in the native proposal and run that comparator once
successfully after approval. Do not run the other mode or report an expected failure
as validation. Retain the selected source file with the other observed artifacts.

# Using zeroh-greenfield

Inspect the repository before choosing exactly one route; return the dispatch contract below and do not execute the routed workflow.
Not this skill: delegate routed work to `greenfield-init`, `brownfield-audit`, or `stack-decision`; keep only initial trigger routing here. Use `roadmap/arc-evals/phase-29.peval.json` as the 2026-09-04 delivery evidence.

## Dispatch

| Request | Skill |
| --- | --- |
| init / new repo / scaffold | greenfield-init |
| audit / fill gaps / brownfield | brownfield-audit |
| stack choice / mobile stack | stack-decision |

Return exactly one object:

```json
{"route":"greenfield-init|brownfield-audit|stack-decision","evidence":["<repository-relative-path>"]}
```

Define `<repository-relative-path>` as an inspected marker path. If inspection cannot resolve the repository root, STOP with `route: unresolved` and the attempted path; this STOP is honor-system.

## Detection markers

Treat any existing marker as brownfield evidence. When markers disagree, use
`brownfield-audit`; it preserves existing homes and proposes only gaps.
Apply the canonical detection procedure in `../brownfield-audit/references/marker-table.md`; its root resolver refusal enforces ambiguous-root failure, while route selection remains honor-system.

| Marker | Greenfield | Brownfield |
| --- | --- | --- |
| package-manager locks | absent | one or more present |
| framework files | absent | framework config or source present |
| existing docs | absent | product, architecture, UX, or standards docs present |
| harness files | absent | AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, or another agent harness present |
| roadmap config | no marked root | canonical resolver finds a marked root or config (see `../brownfield-audit/references/marker-table.md`) |

## Ownership boundaries

- Delegate post-initialization phase planning and execution to `zeroh-roadmap`; prepare only the consumer homes and pointers it needs.
- Delegate Blade tokens, themes, and branded design work to `zeroh-design`; record only its pointers.
- Keep the trigger map in this router. Treat both ownership rules as honor-system; each routed skill names this router as the reverse boundary.

name: greenfield-init
description: Handle requests phrased as initialize, scaffold, or create a new repository through an approval-gated setup with sourced stack, design, standards, and roadmap pointers.
---

# Greenfield initialization

Use this workflow only after `using-zeroh-greenfield` finds no brownfield
markers. Load each reference only at the step that names it.
Not this skill: route initial trigger selection through `using-zeroh-greenfield`, repositories with existing markers through `brownfield-audit`, and alternative selection through `stack-decision`. Use `roadmap/arc-evals/phase-32.peval.json` as the 2026-09-04 initialized-home evidence.

## Read-only compatibility preflight

Before the interview, proposal, approval request, generator, or any consumer write,
require `roadmap` and run `roadmap config capabilities --json`. The response must be
valid JSON with `configVersion: 1`, `scopeManifestProtocol:
"scope-manifest-json-v1"`, and slots `unit-scoped`, `unit-affected`, and
`unit-impacted`. If the command is absent, exits nonzero, returns malformed or older
capabilities, print `/plugin install zeroh-roadmap@zeroh-marketplace` and STOP with
zero consumer writes.
Before approval, run only that named roadmap command; specifically do not invoke `roadmap init`, including `roadmap init --help`. The CLI command-help dispatch keeps `roadmap init --help` read-only; `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs` later rejects any observed preapproval mutation.

## Interview

Load `references/prd-interview.md`. Ask one question at a time and retain
unknowns. Do not write the PRD yet.

Invoke `zeroh-greenfield:stack-decision` after the platforms and constraints
are known. It owns the stack alternatives and decision-record text.

## Draft proposal

Load these references in order and assemble a complete proposal:

1. `references/design-system.md` for the design-system choice or sibling handoff.
2. `references/archetypes/<name>.md` for the chosen generator and file shape, where `<name>` is `web`, `flutter`, `android`, `expo`, `nx-monorepo`, or `library-cli`.
3. `references/standards.md` for repository conventions and documentation.

Present every proposed operation in this exact table:

| Artifact | Target | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <artifact-or-command> | <consumer-path> | <why-it-is-needed> |

Include generator commands as artifacts. Cover the PRD,
decision records, design pointers, archetype, standards, harness files, README,
and roadmap configuration before requesting approval.

Also emit this parser-bound object with concrete values and exactly the seven gate keys:

```json
{"type":"proposal","artifacts":[{"path":"<repository-relative-path>","reason":"<reason>"}],"commands":[{"command":"<command>"}],"gates":{"lint":"<command-or-none>","types":"<command-or-none>","unit":"<command-or-none>","integration":"<command-or-none>","build":"<command-or-none>","e2e":"<command-or-none>","emit":"<command-or-none>"}}
```

Define paths relative to the consumer root, reasons as non-empty approval rationale, and `none` as an approved absence with its reason in the proposal table. `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs` rejects unsafe, broad, duplicate, or unproposed artifact paths.

## Approval gate

Ask for the exact response `APPROVE GREENFIELD PLAN`.

STOP before any write or generator run unless that exact response follows the
complete proposal. Do not interpret partial agreement as approval. Record the
approved plan and response in `docs/PRD.md §Decisions` during execution.
Treat this gate as enforced by `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs`; other approval interpretation is honor-system.

If a Blade brand requires the design sibling and it is absent, show
`/plugin install zeroh-design@zeroh-marketplace` and STOP that branch. Do not
substitute either sibling's work.

## Execute approved plan

Execute only approved rows through the following headings in order. Run the selected archetype generator first, then write the PRD, decision records, standards, architecture and UX indexes, and harness adapters.

## Structure

Populate README structure from the selected manifest's `## File tree` and
approved `## Generator` and `## Post-steps` outputs.

## Commands

Populate README commands from the selected manifest’s `## Verify` and test conventions.
Resolve `templates/scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs` from the installed zeroh-greenfield plugin root, copy it to consumer path `scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs`, and run the selected manifest checker.
Record its exit code before Done.


## Roadmap configuration

Run `roadmap init`, then apply only the keys from `references/pointers.md`.

Never replace an existing home discovered after approval. Stop with the changed
evidence and draft a revised proposal instead.

## Verify

Follow `references/pointers.md` to execute every non-`none` gate from the consumer root, recording cwd/exit and approved absence reasons. Run the selected archetype's Verify command, the README catalog check, and
`roadmap config check`. Report each command and exit status. A failing command
keeps the initialization incomplete.

## Done

Return Done only when every approved artifact exists, every unapproved path is unchanged,
the approval ruling is in the PRD, the catalog check passes, and
`roadmap config check` exits `0`. Report the artifact paths and verification
results; do not use a prose-only success claim.

After auditing the completed tree, emit `{"type":"audit-result","proposals":[],"writes":[],"gaps":[]}` only when the skill proposes and writes nothing. `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs` later cross-checks the claim against independent observer events and tree snapshots; treat other STOP and preservation instructions as honor-system.

# Brownfield marker table

Inspect every row. Evidence supports classification but absence never proves a stack.

| Artefact | Evidence glob | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Package managers | `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `package-lock.json`, `uv.lock`, `pubspec.yaml`, `gradlew` | Present files identify installed package tooling; conflicting locks are partial or stale evidence. |
| Framework files | `next.config.*`, `app.json`, `android/`, `pubspec.yaml`, `vite.config.*` | Framework-owned configuration supports a candidate stack that stack-decision must confirm. |
| Monorepo tools | `nx.json`, `turbo.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `lerna.json` | Existing workspace orchestration is preserved and linked. |
| Docs | `README.md`, `docs/**/*.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` | Existing fact homes are inventoried before proposing a missing index or canon. |
| Harness files | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.cursor/rules/**`, `.codex/**`, `opencode.json` | Apply the harness inventory and generated-block preservation contract. |
| Roadmap config | `roadmap/roadmap.config.json`, `roadmap/phases/`, `docs/roadmap/roadmap.config.json`, `docs/roadmap/phases/`, the explicit `ROADMAP_ROOT` path | Existing roadmap configuration is merged, never reinitialized. |
| Superpowers directory | `.superpowers/`, `docs/superpowers/` | Existing planning artifacts are linked rather than duplicated. |
| Design-system files | `components.json`, `**/components.json`, `tokens/**`, `**/*theme*`, `docs/**/*design*` | Registries and token homes are evidence for design reconciliation, not permission to invent values. |

## Canonical roadmap discovery
Resolve the consumer Git toplevel first. Use `roadmapRoot(consumerRoot)` from the
installed zeroh-roadmap `cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs`; resolve that module from the
installed plugin, never from an assumed consumer-relative plugin directory.
Pass the consumer root explicitly, retain `ROADMAP_ROOT`, and inspect
`<resolved root>/roadmap.config.json`. Do not infer absence from a top-level glob.
A marked root without a config is partial: STOP for an approved recovery proposal,
not fresh initialization. Ambiguous roots STOP with the resolver's remedy; an
explicit override retains the resolver's precedence. If the module cannot be
resolved, STOP the config branch with the sibling installation remedy rather than
implementing another candidate-order algorithm. An unmarked default destination
is not an existing configuration. Record the resolved path as gap-table evidence.

Use this read-only invocation after resolving the two absolute paths from the
installed plugin inventory and consumer Git toplevel:

```sh
node --input-type=module -e 'import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url"; import { join } from "node:path"; const { roadmapRoot } = await import(pathToFileURL(join(process.argv[1], "cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs"))); console.log(roadmapRoot(process.argv[2]));' <roadmap-plugin-root> <consumer-root>
```

`<roadmap-plugin-root>` is the installed zeroh-roadmap plugin directory;
`<consumer-root>` is the consumer Git toplevel. A nonzero exit stops this branch.
/**
 * roadmap-root — THE answer to "where is this consumer's roadmap?", and the ONLY module
 * under cli/ or hooks/ allowed to spell the root as a literal (cli/lib/roadmap-root.test.mjs
 * scans for it; every other site joins onto what these functions return).
 *
 * Two homes, discovered rather than configured: the config lives INSIDE the root, so a
 * roadmap.config.json key could never name it. `roadmap/` at the git toplevel is what every
 * consumer has today and stays first; `docs/roadmap/` is the second candidate, for a repo that
 * keeps its workflows as sibling doc folders (docs/roadmap/ beside docs/superpowers/).
 *
 * The rules, in order:
 *  - ROADMAP_ROOT wins, absolute or resolved against `dir`, and is NOT probed — an override
 *    names where the root WILL be, so `roadmap init` can scaffold into it.
 *  - else the first candidate carrying a MARKER (roadmap.config.json or phases/). An existing
 *    but unmarked directory is not a marker: a repo with a prose docs/roadmap/ folder must
 *    keep reading its real roadmap/.
 *  - both marked → RoadmapRootError('ambiguous'), never a silent pick. Two roots means two
 *    backlogs, two claim registries and two gate directories; guessing one is how half a
 *    consumer's records go quietly unread.
 *  - neither marked → the default first candidate, so a fresh or non-consumer tree answers
 *    exactly what it answered before this module existed.
 *
 * SHELL TWIN: hooks/lib/roadmap-root.sh implements the same three rules for the hooks, which
 * cannot afford to spawn node on every tool call. A change here is a change there. It differs in
 * FORM only on ambiguity — it returns non-zero after one stderr line instead of throwing, because
 * a hook must never block a session — and in neither case does either twin GUESS a root.
 */
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join, resolve, relative, isAbsolute, sep } from 'node:path'
import { BridgeError } from './bridge-error.mjs'
import { gitToplevel } from './gitroot.mjs'

/** The root homes, in PRECEDENCE order. Extending this list extends discovery everywhere. */
export const ROOT_CANDIDATES = ['roadmap', 'docs/roadmap']

/** What makes a candidate directory a roadmap root rather than a same-named prose folder. */
const MARKERS = ['roadmap.config.json', 'phases']

/** Typed root-resolution failure. kind ∈ 'ambiguous'. Same shape as ConfigError. */
export class RoadmapRootError extends Error {
  constructor(kind, messageLines) {
    super(messageLines.join('\n'))
    this.name = 'RoadmapRootError'
    this.kind = kind
    this.messageLines = messageLines
  }
}

/** [dir, override] → resolved root. Keyed on both: a memo keyed on dir alone
 *  would hand a later caller an answer the current ROADMAP_ROOT never authorized. */
const memo = new Map()

/**
 * Drop every memoized resolution. For tests and long-lived processes that MUTATE a tree
 * (scaffolding a root, then resolving it) — the probes are fs reads, and a cached miss
 * outlives the directory that caused it.
 */
export function resetRoadmapRootCache() {
  memo.clear()
}

/** The override in force, or null. An empty ROADMAP_ROOT is unset, not "the cwd". */
function override() {
  const raw = process.env.ROADMAP_ROOT
  return raw != null && raw !== '' ? raw : null
}

const isRoot = (candidateDir) => MARKERS.some((m) => existsSync(join(candidateDir, m)))

/**
 * The consumer's roadmap data root for the tree at `dir` (normally a git toplevel).
 * @param {string} dir
 * @returns {string} an ABSOLUTE directory path
 * @throws {RoadmapRootError} kind 'ambiguous' when more than one candidate is marked
 */
export function roadmapRoot(dir) {
  const env = override()
  const key = JSON.stringify([dir, env])
  const hit = memo.get(key)
  if (hit !== undefined) return hit

  // The override is checked BEFORE the ambiguity refusal on purpose: it is the remedy that
  // refusal advertises, and a remedy resolved after the throw could never be taken.
  const resolved = env ? (isAbsolute(env) ? env : resolve(dir, env)) : probe(dir)
  memo.set(key, resolved)
  return resolved
}

function probe(dir) {
  const marked = ROOT_CANDIDATES.map((c) => resolve(dir, c)).filter(isRoot)
  if (marked.length > 1) {
    throw new RoadmapRootError('ambiguous', [
      `roadmap: ${dir} carries more than one roadmap root — ${marked.join(' and ')}`,
      `each holds its own records, so reading either one silently hides the other. Delete or merge the one that is not yours, or name the real root: ROADMAP_ROOT=<dir> roadmap <command>`,
    ])
  }
  return marked[0] ?? resolve(dir, ROOT_CANDIDATES[0])
}

/**
 * The root a FLAGLESS `roadmap status` / `roadmap claim` reads: the consumer's resolved root.
 * Outside a git repo — where both commands still accept a bare roadmap directory — the
 * candidate under `cwd`.
 *
 * ONLY the not-a-repo case falls back. A RoadmapRootError must ESCAPE: falling back on an
 * ambiguous tree would resolve `<cwd>/roadmap` and silently pick one of the two roots the
 * refusal exists to prevent — and from a SUBDIRECTORY it would invent a root that is not
 * there at all.
 * @param {string} cwd
 * @returns {string} an ABSOLUTE directory path
 * @throws {RoadmapRootError} kind 'ambiguous', unchanged, from either branch
 */
export function defaultRoadmapRoot(cwd) {
  let toplevel
  try {
    toplevel = gitToplevel(cwd)
  } catch {
    return roadmapRoot(cwd)
  }
  return roadmapRoot(toplevel)
}

/**
 * The same answer spelled RELATIVE to `dir`, POSIX-separated and with no trailing slash —
 * what git pathspecs (`git log -- <rel>/backlog.ts`), diff-path prefix tests and the
 * repo-relative provenance strings cited in eval reports all need. Throws exactly where
 * roadmapRoot throws: an ambiguous tree must never be handed a guessed pathspec.
 * @param {string} dir
 * @returns {string} e.g. 'roadmap' or 'docs/roadmap'
 */
export function roadmapRootRel(dir) {
  const rel = relative(dir, roadmapRoot(dir))
  return sep === '/' ? rel : rel.split(sep).join('/')
}

/**
 * The consumer's vendored schema seam — what the tsx bridge validates every typed roadmap
 * file through. Root-first (`<root>/lib/schema.ts`, what a consumer scaffolded from now on
 * carries, reachable by a relative import with no tsconfig alias), then the LEGACY
 * `<dir>/lib/roadmap/schema.ts` that every existing consumer still has.
 * @param {string} dir  a consumer root (git toplevel)
 * @returns {string} an absolute path to an existing file
 * @throws {BridgeError} kind 'schema-missing', naming BOTH candidates
 */
export function consumerSchemaPath(dir) {
  const rootSeam = join(roadmapRoot(dir), 'lib', 'schema.ts')
  if (existsSync(rootSeam)) return rootSeam
  const legacySeam = join(dir, 'lib', 'roadmap', 'schema.ts')
  if (existsSync(legacySeam)) return legacySeam
  throw new BridgeError('schema-missing', [
    `roadmap: no consumer schema at ${rootSeam} (nor at the legacy seam ${legacySeam}) — this repo is not a roadmap consumer`,
  ])
}

Ask one question at a time. Accept `Don't know yet` without filling in an

# Stack decision

Load `references/matrices.md`. Determine which matrices apply from the approved
PRD answers, then present every row in each applicable matrix unchanged.
Not this skill: route initial trigger selection through `using-zeroh-greenfield`, leave repository changes to `greenfield-init` or `brownfield-audit`, and return only `StackDecisionOutput` here. Use `roadmap/arc-evals/phase-30.peval.json` as the 2026-09-04 delivery evidence.

## Selection

Ask exactly one selection question per applicable matrix.
Do not preselect any option before the user answers.
Present the backend matrix ONLY when the PRD answers name an API.

Accept an explicit named option or a request to revisit requirements. Do not
infer a choice from preferences. When the user chooses, ask for or summarize the
reason and confirm it before producing the ruling.

/**
 * roadmap init [--config] [--scaffold] [--root <dir>] — bare init = scaffold then config.
 *  --scaffold execs the plugin's OWN scripts/scaffold-roadmap.sh (the proven copier;
 *    ONE implementation — never a node port beside the living bash).
 *  --root is forwarded to the scaffold (default `roadmap`; `docs/roadmap` is the other
 *    candidate cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs discovers). It is NOT a config key: the config lives
 *    inside the root it would have to name.
 *  --config writes roadmap.config.json under roadmapRoot(toplevel) — RESOLVED, and resolved
 *    AFTER scaffolding so `--root docs/roadmap` lands the config beside what was just created
 *    ($schema → relative path to the plugin schema, configVersion 1, the seven core
 *    gateCommands slots with honest placeholders). REFUSES (exit 1) if the file already exists
 *    — never clobber a consumer's config. init writes no optional blocks: absent mergePolicy
 *    = hold-for-user is the safe default by construction.
 */
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { existsSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join, dirname, relative, resolve } from 'node:path'
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
import { gitToplevel } from '../lib/gitroot.mjs'
import { roadmapRoot, resetRoadmapRootCache } from '../lib/roadmap-root.mjs'

const SCAFFOLD_SH = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../scripts/scaffold-roadmap.sh', import.meta.url))
const SCHEMA_ABS = fileURLToPath(new URL('../roadmap.config.schema.json', import.meta.url))

const PLACEHOLDER_CONFIG = {
  gateCommands: {
    lint: 'npm run lint',
    types: 'npm run type-check',
    unit: 'npm test',
    integration: 'npm run test:integration',
    build: 'npm run build',
    e2e: 'npm run test:e2e',
    emit: 'npm run emit:phases',
  },
}

export default async function run(argv) {
  const wantScaffold = argv.includes('--scaffold')
  const wantConfig = argv.includes('--config')
  const both = !wantScaffold && !wantConfig // bare init runs both

  const rootIdx = argv.indexOf('--root')
  const root = rootIdx >= 0 ? argv[rootIdx + 1] : undefined
  if (rootIdx >= 0 && (!root || root.startsWith('--'))) {
    process.stderr.write('roadmap init: --root needs a directory (e.g. --root docs/roadmap)\n')
    return 1
  }

  const toplevel = gitToplevel(process.cwd())

  if (both || wantScaffold) {
    try {
      execFileSync('bash', [SCAFFOLD_SH, toplevel, ...(root ? ['--root', root] : [])], { stdio: 'inherit' })
    } catch {
      return 1 // the scaffold refused (a second root) and has already said why on stderr
    }
    // The scaffold just CREATED the root; a resolution memoized before it existed would send the
    // config to the pre-scaffold answer.
    resetRoadmapRootCache()
  }

  if (both || wantConfig) {
    const configPath = join(root ? resolve(toplevel, root) : roadmapRoot(toplevel), 'roadmap.config.json')
    if (existsSync(configPath)) {
      process.stderr.write(
        `roadmap init: ${configPath} already exists — refusing to clobber a consumer's config\n`,
      )
      return 1
    }
    mkdirSync(dirname(configPath), { recursive: true })
    const config = {
      $schema: relative(dirname(configPath), SCHEMA_ABS),
      configVersion: 1,
      ...PLACEHOLDER_CONFIG,
    }
    writeFileSync(configPath, JSON.stringify(config, null, 2) + '\n')
    process.stderr.write(`roadmap init: wrote ${configPath}\n`)
  }

  return 0
}
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scaffold-roadmap.sh — Initialize phase-driven roadmap in a project
#
# Usage: scaffold-roadmap.sh [PROJECT_DIR] [--root <dir>]
#   --root defaults to `roadmap`; `--root docs/roadmap` puts the whole consumer under
#   docs/roadmap/ beside a sibling docs folder. Everything lands UNDER the root, including the
#   schema seam — which is what lets a phase file import `../lib/schema` relatively, with no
#   tsconfig path alias. The legacy toplevel `lib/roadmap/schema.ts` seam stays recognized by
#   cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs, so existing consumers are untouched.
#
# Creates (<root> = --root, default `roadmap`):
#   <root>/lib/schema.ts     — definePhase() + Zod shapes
#   <root>/lib/registry.ts   — Phase discovery (dynamic import + validation)
#   <root>/lib/emit.ts       — Registry emission (deterministic JSON + digest)
#   <root>/ROADMAP.md        — Validation gate + git strategy
#   <root>/backlog.ts        — Ordered execution queue
#   <root>/phases/           — Empty phases directory
#   reviews/releases/         — Release review reports directory
#   scripts/pre-review.sh     — Automated pre-review checks
#   scripts/build-dashboard.sh — Review dashboard HTML generator

set -euo pipefail

PLUGIN_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
PROJECT_DIR="."
ROOT="roadmap"
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --root)
      ROOT="${2:?--root needs a directory}"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --root=*)
      ROOT="${1#--root=}"
      shift
      ;;
    *)
      PROJECT_DIR="$1"
      shift
      ;;
  esac
done

# REFUSE rather than create a second root. Two marked roots is the ambiguity
# cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs refuses to resolve, so scaffolding one into existence would hand the
# consumer a repo no command can read. A marker is roadmap.config.json or phases/ — the same
# two the resolver probes.
for candidate in roadmap docs/roadmap; do
  [ "$candidate" = "$ROOT" ] && continue
  if [ -f "$PROJECT_DIR/$candidate/roadmap.config.json" ] || [ -d "$PROJECT_DIR/$candidate/phases" ]; then
    echo "scaffold-roadmap: $PROJECT_DIR already carries a roadmap root at $candidate — refusing to create a second one at $ROOT." >&2
    echo "  Two roots means two backlogs and two registries, and every command would refuse to pick between them. Scaffold into $candidate, or move it first." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

echo "=== Scaffolding zeroh-roadmap in $PROJECT_DIR (root: $ROOT) ==="

# Create directories
mkdir -p "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/lib"
mkdir -p "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/phases"
mkdir -p "$PROJECT_DIR/reviews/releases"
mkdir -p "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts"

# Copy <root>/lib templates — schema, registry, emit. This is the seam a phase file reaches with
# a RELATIVE `../lib/schema`; no tsconfig `paths` alias is required of the consumer.
for lib_file in schema.ts registry.ts emit.ts; do
  if [ ! -f "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/lib/$lib_file" ]; then
    cp "$PLUGIN_DIR/templates/$lib_file" "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/lib/$lib_file"
    echo "  Created $ROOT/lib/$lib_file"
  else
    echo "  Skipped $ROOT/lib/$lib_file (already exists)"
  fi
done

# Copy ROADMAP.md
if [ ! -f "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/ROADMAP.md" ]; then
  cp "$PLUGIN_DIR/templates/ROADMAP.md" "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/ROADMAP.md"
  echo "  Created $ROOT/ROADMAP.md"
else
  echo "  Skipped $ROOT/ROADMAP.md (already exists)"
fi

# Copy backlog.ts (ordered execution queue)
if [ ! -f "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/backlog.ts" ]; then
  cp "$PLUGIN_DIR/templates/backlog.ts" "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/backlog.ts"
  echo "  Created $ROOT/backlog.ts"
else
  echo "  Skipped $ROOT/backlog.ts (already exists)"
fi

# Scaffold roadmap/arcs/ (OPT-IN — arcs are optional; defineArc rides along via schema.ts).
# Deliberately NOT in audit REQUIRED_ARTIFACTS: a repo without arcs is fully valid.
# The directory only, never an example arc file: anything landing here is a LIVE arc, so a
# copied example makes id A with phases [1] real in a consumer that has authored none.
# templates/example.arc.ts stays installed with the plugin as reference material.
mkdir -p "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/arcs"

# Copy scripts
for script in pre-review.sh build-dashboard.sh generate-changelog-md.ts; do
  if [ ! -f "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/$script" ]; then
    if [ -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/scripts/$script" ]; then
      cp "$PLUGIN_DIR/scripts/$script" "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/$script"
      echo "  Created scripts/$script"
    fi
  else
    echo "  Skipped scripts/$script (already exists)"
  fi
done

# Make shell scripts executable
chmod +x "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/"*.sh 2>/dev/null || true

# Wire the npm scripts the skills invoke. do-phase / plan-phase / full-code-review all run
# `<pm> emit:phases` to regenerate reviews/changelog.json; without this script the agent can't
# find it and skips the regen. Idempotent: existing scripts are left untouched.
if [ -f "$PROJECT_DIR/package.json" ]; then
  node - "$PROJECT_DIR/package.json" "$ROOT" <<'NODE'
const fs = require('fs');
const path = process.argv[2];
const pkg = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path, 'utf8'));
pkg.scripts = pkg.scripts || {};
const root = process.argv[3];
const want = {
  'emit:phases': `tsx ${root}/lib/emit.ts`,
  'changelog:md': 'tsx scripts/generate-changelog-md.ts',
};
let changed = false;
